metadata.title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis - Thermo Fisher UltraPure Agarose
metadata.purpose: Common nucleic acid analysis workflow for PCR products, plasmid digests, and restriction fragments.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current manufacturer protocol, SDS, and local EHS rules before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Select agarose percentage based on expected fragment size. Higher agarose resolves smaller fragments; lower agarose resolves larger fragments.
Use the same buffer for gel casting and running to avoid distorted migration.
Confirm stain compatibility with downstream cloning. Use safer alternatives or blue light when extracting DNA.
Check that the gel is level, wells are intact, and buffer covers the gel by a thin layer.

materials.name: 1X electrophoresis buffer such as TAE or TBE
materials.specification: Use the same buffer for gel casting and running to avoid distorted migration

equipment.name: Power supply
equipment.settings: Run at the selected voltage until dye front reaches the appropriate distance

equipment.settings: Use the correct excitation and emission settings

equipment.name: Blue-light transilluminator
equipment.settings: Optional; to reduce DNA damage when bands will be excised

rows: Electrodes reversed, power off, or wrong chamber setup.

steps.action: Prepare agarose in the selected 1X running buffer and dissolve completely by heating. Avoid boil-over.
Cool molten agarose to about 50-60 deg C before adding stain if using in-gel stain.

parameters.rawText: Cool molten agarose to about 50-60 deg C before adding stain if using in-gel stain.

steps.action: Pour gel into the casting tray with comb installed. Remove bubbles and allow gel to solidify fully.
steps.expectedResult: Fully solidified gel with intact wells and no bubbles.

steps.action: Place gel in electrophoresis chamber and cover with 1X running buffer.
Mix DNA samples with loading dye unless already prepared in loading buffer.
Load ladder into at least one lane and load samples carefully without puncturing wells.
Confirm wells are near the negative electrode so DNA migrates toward the positive electrode.
steps.criticalNotes: Confirm electrode orientation before starting electrophoresis or transfer. DNA/RNA generally migrates toward the positive electrode; SDS-coated proteins migrate toward the anode.

steps.action: Run at the selected voltage until dye front reaches the appropriate distance.
Image the gel using the correct excitation and emission settings.
Save image file with date, gel ID, ladder, sample map, and exposure settings.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expected ladder bands should be sharp and in correct order.
Samples should migrate in the expected direction and show minimal smiling or lane leakage.

steps.expectedResult: Use gel image for size estimation, purity assessment, or band excision notes.

controls.name: DNA ladder
controls.description: Load ladder into at least one lane. Expected ladder bands should be sharp and in correct order.

expectedOutputs: Expected ladder bands should be sharp and in correct order.
Samples should migrate in the expected direction and show minimal smiling or lane leakage.
Use gel image for size estimation, purity assessment, or band excision notes.
For cloning-grade DNA, minimize UV exposure and document excision band size.

Lower voltage, use fresh buffer, cast gel level.

troubleshooting.solution: Check stain and imager settings; load more DNA or image longer.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Treat gels, membranes, stains, acrylamide, methanol, formaldehyde, UV exposure, and radioactive/nonradioactive probes according to local EHS rules.
Use a fume hood for formaldehyde, methanol, chloroform-like solvents, powdered stains, and hazardous probe/detection reagents when required.
Acrylamide monomer is neurotoxic before polymerization. Use appropriate PPE and dispose of unpolymerized acrylamide waste correctly.
Confirm electrode orientation before starting electrophoresis or transfer. DNA/RNA generally migrates toward the positive electrode; SDS-coated proteins migrate toward the anode.
Record gel percentage, buffer system, voltage/current, run time, stain/probe/antibody details, membrane type, exposure, image file, and deviations.
